channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: ESPN’s Jeremy Fowler reports that Rams OG Bill Murray ruptured his Achilles tendon in the Rams’ Week 12 win over the Packers.
item.description: This is unfortunate. Murray, a backup, started at left guard and played well. He will now undergo surgery and begin rehab for the 2027 NFL season. The Rams’ offensive line is fairly banged up. Hopefully, the extra time off allows the unit to improve its health.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: NFL on Prime’s James Palmer believes Brian Schottenheimer will remain the Cowboys’ head coach for the rest of the season.
item.description: Palmer’s report wasn’t entirely positive. He also believes that if the Cowboys’ performance does not improve, “there are going to be some decisions that Jerry Jones needs to make after the season.” It sounds like Schottenheimer may be coaching for his job for the rest of the year. Stay tuned.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Drew Lock (elbow) is not on the Seahawks’ final injury report for Week 12 against the 49ers.
item.description: Lock was limited again this week with tendinitis in his throwing arm’s elbow. With Sam Darnold (quad) back in action, Lock returns to his backup role.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Harold Fannin (groin) is not on the Browns’ final injury report and will play in Week 12 against the Raiders.
item.description: Fannin upgraded to full participation on Thursday and remained at that level today. Fannin has dealt with this groin issue for a couple of weeks, but still posted a 7/91 receiving line last week. He is a locked-in TE1 against a soft Raiders defense.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Evan Engram didn’t catch either of his two targets in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
item.description: Engram was a complete non-factor, which is particularly disappointing after his six-catch, 74-yard effort in Week 11 against the Raiders. Unfortunately, this is much more inline with his previous production, and Engram can safely be ignored in Week 13 against the Dolphins.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Pat Freiermuth caught his only target for one yard in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
item.description: Freiermuth didn’t have his first target until the beginning of the fourth quarter. The 28-year-old was a consistent target of Aaron Rodgers, but he didn’t appear to have much of a rapport with Mason Rudolph in their first game together. Freiermuth can’t be trusted as more than a low-end TE2 for Week 13 against the Texans.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Pat Bryant caught 4-of-7 targets for 42 yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
item.description: Bryant was able to make the most of an unfathomably bad day from Bo Nix, although it’s far from a fantasy stat line fantasy managers are clamoring for. Bryant has been one of the more consistent options for the Denver passing attack, but that’s not the compliment it should be. Bryant is at best a FLEX for Week 13 against the Dolphins.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Courtland Sutton caught 1-of-8 targets for four yards in the Broncos’ Week 12 loss to the Steelers.
item.description: To be fair to Sutton, Bo Nix was trying to get him the football. To be honest, he didn’t. Sutton was once among the better wideout options, but he’s been consistently putting up duds like this for too long in 2026 to count on him in fantasy. Even in a friendly matchup against the Dolphins in Week 13, fantasy managers should be looking elsewhere.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Rico Dowdle rushed 11 times for 71 yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos while catching one pass for three yards.
item.description: Dowdle was the much more effective runner between he and Jaylen Warren, although the bulk of the yardage came on one 27-yard scoot. He also lost a fumble, but the Steelers still gave him some carries after that turnover. A solid yardage day, but fantasy managers shouldn’t expect similar production in Week 13 against the Texans.- Christopher Crawford

item.title: Michael Pittman caught 1-of-2 targets for seven yards in the Steelers’ Week 12 win over the Broncos.
item.description: Pittman was playing in his first game since Week 4, and he — and most of the Pittsburgh offense — didn’t have much chemistry with Mason Rudolph in a game where the Steelers’ defense was their best offense. The former Colt could be an option in the coming weeks, but shouldn’t be trusted in Week 13 against the Texans.- Christopher Crawford
